known_issues: The top-level audio_seconds and frames fields mixed sides: audio_seconds was the reference's 51.88 s while frames was ours (1451, i.e. 58.04 s of audio). The two sides produced different amounts of audio, so the elapsed ratio in the first reading of this artifact (172.45 s against 137.80 s = 1.25x) is not like for like; the real-time-factor ratio (1.12x) compares different outputs too and is reported only as context.

The bandwidth analysis published with this artifact counted the whole 7.26 GB checkpoint as the AR stage's per-step read. The checkpoint also carries the acoustic weights, and one AR branch reads ~3.57 GB per step (28 layers of q/k/v/o/gate/up/down plus the 756 MB output head), so two serial branch forwards read ~7.15 GB per token, not 13 GB. At 82.13 ms per token that is ~87 GB/s of weight traffic against the reference's ~114 GB/s, both far below this host's ~256 GB/s peak, so the stage is not at a bandwidth ceiling and branch batching is a candidate to measure rather than the only route.

The 154.1 s whole-path figure was a linear frame normalisation of our 172.45 s run to the reference's 1 297 frames, presented as a measured end-to-end. It is an estimate and is withdrawn; frame-normalising attention-heavy work is not valid.
